title: Shadow validation and orchestrated deprecation for API streaming, tool calls, and structured outputs
text:
Shadow validation and orchestrated deprecation for API streaming, tool calls, and structured outputs

description:
This ticket defines the product-led plan to introduce a staged deprecation and migration pathway for upcoming API semantic changes affecting streaming responses, function/tool-calling handoffs, and structured output schemas. The approach centers on a dual-run/shadow-validation mode, behavior flags for opt-in semantics, and a customer validation program that produces rigorous backward compatibility test signals before any hard deprecation windows are announced.

objective:
Minimize customer disruption while evolving API semantics. Provide automated safety nets (shadowing, replay tests, fuzzy matching for structured outputs) and a clear timeline, docs, SDK adapters, and telemetry that let customers move to the new behavior at their pace.

background:
We plan to change subtle streaming chunk semantics (metadata gating and token boundary emission), tighten tool-calling guarantees (argument coercion and sync vs async semantics), and evolve structured-output schemas to a stricter typed format. Historically, small behavior differences caused client regressions (websocket stream parsers, SDKs that relied on legacy tool-call edge cases). Several earlier engineering and PM tickets investigated the surface area and instrumented probes (see dependencies and links).

proposed_solution:
1) Implement a runtime shadow-run mode where each live request is executed against both the current GA contract and the new contract. 2) Emit side-by-side diffs into a validation store and run deterministic replay checks nightly. 3) Expose granular behavior-flags at the API key and route level (server-side toggles) so customers can opt their keys into new semantics. 4) Provide client-side SDK adapters that translate legacy expectations to the new responses when feasible. 5) Maintain a compatibility replayer and test harness that runs customer prompt fixtures to surface regressions programmatically.

rollout_plan:
Phase 0 — Instrumentation (2 weeks): build shadow-run hooks, validation store schema, and telemetry events for diffs.
Phase 1 — Internal Trials (2 weeks): enable shadow mode for internal teams + sample enterprise tenants; run nightly replays and produce weekly regression reports.
Phase 2 — Early Adopters (4 weeks): invite opt-in customers to join migration cohort; provide SDK adapters and migration guides; collect feedback and compatibility metrics.
Phase 3 — Broad Opt-in Flags (2 weeks): flip behavior flags to be available to all customers as opt-in; continue monitoring and extend SDKs for more languages.
Phase 4 — Announce Deprecation Window (6+ weeks after stable metrics): publish final timeline for mandatory migration and provide one-click upgrade paths in Console and CLI.
Phase 5 — Enforcement & Cleanup: retire legacy code paths and remove behavior flags after successful migrations and a minimum notice period.

testing_plan:
Develop a replay harness that can run stored customer prompt fixtures against both old and new runtimes and emit a signed result summary.
Create a diffs classification pipeline (benign, formatting-only, breaking) using a rule-based + ML classifier; tune thresholds with internal datasets.
Integrate backcompat tests into CI to run on every runtime or API change candidate; block merges on high-severity regressions.
Add E2E tests for streaming behavior (chunk boundaries, finalization events) in the SDK matrix (Node, Python, Go, Java).
Smoke tests for tool-calling change surface: argument coercion scenarios, error propagation, idempotency edges.

telemetry_and_alerts:
Validation mismatch rate (per-customer, per-route) with time-series and percentiles.
Number of unique prompts that produced a breaking-classified diff in the last 7 days.
Spike alert if mismatch rate > 0.5% for P0 customers or >2% cluster-wide for >24h.
Weekly compatibility health dashboard in Console and an exportable CSV for solutions teams.
Audit trail events for flag flips (who, when, before/after snapshot link).

communications:
Pre-announcement to enterprise account managers with migration kit and timeline proposal.
Public migration guide published in Docs with code snippets for SDK adapters and examples for streaming parsers.
Console banners for customers with affected usage patterns (streaming/tool-calls) offering a guided migration workflow.
Webinars and office hours for cohort customers during Early Adopter phase.
Standard deprecation email templates and a dedicated migration channel for support tickets.

dependencies:
ENG-7031-behavior-toggles-and-backcompat-test-harness
ENG-8422-continuity-gate-phased-opt-in-flags-regression-suite
PM-31876-evolution-safety-fallbacks
ENG-45677-deprecation-safety-net-probes-and-replayer

risks:
False positives in diff classifier may block safe rollouts and erode trust — mitigation: human-in-the-loop review for first 2 weeks.
High storage/compute cost of shadow runs if enabled broadly — mitigation: sampled shadowing and quota-based limits per tenant.
Customer confusion from parallel behaviors across SDK versions — mitigation: clear labeling, SDK adapters, and console flag controls.
Edge-case regressions in streaming parsers (partial chunks) could leak to low-latency customers — mitigation: stricter canaries and realtime alerts.

acceptance_criteria:
Shadow-run validation pipeline is deployed to staging and captures diffs for 100% of targeted routes.
Diff classifier reaches <5% benign false-positive rate on internal benchmarks.
Two production Early Adopter customers complete migration with no P1 incidents for 30 days.
SDK adapters for Node and Python available as previews and documented in migration guide.
Console shows per-key behavior-flag control and successful audit logs for flips.
